lines.text: Where the Sahara meets the Atlantic, caravan towns kept libraries in the sand. This is the story of Mauritania.
In the eighth century the desert town of Chinguetti was founded, later a holy city of Islam, famous for its old libraries.
In the eleventh century the Almoravids rose from these deserts, Berber warriors who would rule Morocco and Spain and found Marrakesh.
Ouadane grew as a caravan town on the trade routes across the Sahara.
After centuries, France made the land a colony. In 1924 Moktar Ould Daddah was born, who would be the first president.
In 1956 Mohamed Ould Ghazouani was born, president since 2019.
In 1958 work began on Nouakchott, a capital built from scratch for the coming nation.
In 1960 Mauritania won its independence from France.
In 1965 astronauts photographed great rings in its desert from space, the Eye of the Sahara.
In 1976 the coast of Banc d'Arguin became a national park, winter home to millions of birds.
And in 1981 Mauritania became the last country in the world to abolish slavery, though it was made a crime only in 2007.
From the Almoravids to the modern state, Mauritania's story is written in the sand.
